title: "Live vs. Minimal ISO Strategies"

# Live vs. Minimal ISO Strategies

When publishing an operating system, distribution maintainers typically offer two distinct installation image flavors:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|               ISO Distribution Architecture               |
|                                                           |
| Flavor           Live ISO Image          Minimal / NetInstall|
| --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Download Size    ~1.5 GB - 3.5 GB        ~150 MB - 600 MB |
| Desktop Session  Full GUI before install Headless text CLI|
| Offline Install  100% self-contained     Requires Internet|
| Package FreshnessStale packages frozen   Always installs  |
|                  at ISO release date     latest packages  |
| Target Use Case  Desktop trials, repair  Servers, custom  |
|                  workstation rescue      minimal setups   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Strategy 1: The Full Live ISO (Self-Contained)

A **Live ISO** boots directly into an interactive desktop environment (such as Sway or GNOME) running from RAM:
- **Try Before You Install:** Users can test Wi-Fi card compatibility, graphics acceleration, audio drivers, and display scaling before touching their existing hard drives.
- **Offline Reliability:** Contains all packages, compilers, and dependencies. It can be installed on air-gapped computers or remote locations with poor internet connectivity.
- **Rescue Environment:** Serves as a bootable technician's toolkit containing `gparted`, `ddrescue`, `chroot`, `testdisk`, and `fsck`.

## Strategy 2: The Minimal NetInstall ISO

A **NetInstall ISO** contains only the bare-minimum kernel, an initramfs, and the package manager client:
- **Fast Download:** Small download footprint (typically under 250 MB).
- **Zero Package Staleness:** During the installation phase, the installer connects directly to your package repository mirrors over HTTPS and downloads the very latest package releases. When the user reboots into their newly installed machine, zero package updates are pending.
- **Flexible Profiles:** The installer prompts the user with high-level profile options: *"Install Minimal Server"*, *"Install Developer Workstation"*, or *"Install Audio Production DAW"*, downloading only the specific packages chosen.

## Recommendation for BYOL

For the Chapter 13 Capstone Project, we build a **Hybrid Live / Installer ISO**:
- An interactive live environment containing our custom kernel, BusyBox/GNU core tools, and our custom package manager (`byol-pkg`).
- Allows both testing the system in live RAM mode and running an automated installation script (`byol-install`) to format and install the OS onto a permanent disk.
